q: Does a Ruhr steel mill pay CBAM, the EU ETS, or both?
title: Ruhr steel mill: CBAM or EU ETS?
short: The mill pays for its own emissions under the EU ETS. CBAM applies only to goods it imports from outside the EU, such as pig iron, DRI, slabs or ferro-alloys, where it must buy CBAM certificates as the importer. Free allocation under the ETS falls as CBAM phases in from 2026.
audience: Steelworks in the Ruhr and other EU steel regions, and their purchasing teams

p: The EU ETS covers installations inside the EU. CBAM puts the same carbon price on covered goods entering the EU, so imported steel and EU steel face a comparable charge. CBAM certificates are priced on EU ETS auction prices, averaged over the period the Commission publishes for each year.

sections.h: Where CBAM touches an EU mill
ul: Imported precursors: pig iron, DRI, HBI, slabs, billets and covered ferro-alloys.
Imported finished steel the mill trades alongside its own products.
Goods under inward processing that are re-exported are outside CBAM; those released into the EU market are not.

p: Free allocation for CBAM sectors falls from 97.5% of the benchmark-based amount in 2026 to zero in 2034. The same factor reduces the CBAM obligation on imports, so both sides lose their free share on the same schedule.
